'''Rainer Schulin''' (born 22 July 1952) is a German zoologist, [[Forestry|forest scientist]] and [[emeritus]] professor of [[Soil conservation|soil protection]] at the [[ETH Zurich]].<ref>{{Cite web |last=Switzerland |first=Address ETH Zürich Dep of Environmental Systems Science Prof em Dr Rainer Schulin Inst f Terrestrische Oekosysteme CHN F. 73 2 Universitätstrasse 16 8092 Zürich |title=Prof. em. Dr. Rainer Schulin {{!}} ETH Zurich |url=https://ites.ethz.ch/people/person-detail.html |access-date=2023-10-23 |website=ites.ethz.ch |language=en}}</ref>

==Life==
Rainer Schulin studied biology at the [[University of Göttingen]] and graduated at the [[University of Zurich]] in 1976 in zoology. He there completed his PhD thesis in 1981 in zoology and then graduated as a forest engineer at ETH Zurich in 1982.{{citation needed|date=August 2023}} After seven years of research in soil physics he was elected as professor on the newly established ETH Chair of Soil Protection 1990. He has authored or co-authored more than 200 papers in international peer-reviewed journals and is co-author of a German textbook on [[soil ecology]]. Rainer Schulin is married and has a daughter.{{citation needed|date=August 2023}}

==Scientific contributions==
In a model ecosystem experiment Schulin and coworkers showed that soil can play a key role in the growth and [[evapotranspiration]] responses of young forest vegetation on elevated atmospheric [[carbon dioxide]].<ref name="Sonnleitner Günthardt-Goerg Bucher-Wallin Attinger 2001 pp. 271–290">{{cite journal | last1=Sonnleitner | first1=Marion A. | last2=Günthardt-Goerg | first2=Madeleine S. | last3=Bucher-Wallin | first3=Inga K. | last4=Attinger | first4=Werner | last5=Reis | first5=Sybille | last6=Schulin | first6=Rainer |title=Influence of Soil Type on the Effects of Elevated Atmospheric CO2 and N Deposition on the Water Balance and Growth of a Young Spruce and Beech Forest | journal=Water, Air, and Soil Pollution | publisher=Springer Science and Business Media LLC | volume=126 | issue=3/4 | year=2001 | issn=0049-6979 | doi=10.1023/a:1005244916109 | pages=271–290| bibcode=2001WASP..126..271S | s2cid=92078606 | url=https://www.dora.lib4ri.ch/wsl/islandora/object/wsl%3A2272 | hdl=20.500.11850/423126 | hdl-access=free }}</ref> Up to then soil had been neglected as a factor in the response of vegetation to elevated carbon dioxide.

In another model ecosystem experiment Schulin's team found that moderate top[[soil pollution]] by [[heavy metal (chemistry)|heavy metals]] significantly reduced evapotranspiration of a young forest vegetation due to reduced root growth, in particular during periods of [[natural stress#drought|drought stress]], and that roots compensated for metal toxicity in the topsoil by increasing water extraction from the [[subsoil]].<ref name="Menon Hermle Abbaspour Günthardt-Goerg 2005 pp. 227–241">{{cite journal | last1=Menon | first1=Manoj | last2=Hermle | first2=Sandra | last3=Abbaspour | first3=Karim C. | last4=Günthardt-Goerg | first4=Madeleine S. | last5=Oswald | first5=Sascha E. | last6=Schulin | first6=Rainer | title=Water regime of metal-contaminated soil under juvenile forest vegetation | journal=Plant and Soil | publisher=Springer Science and Business Media LLC | volume=271 | issue=1–2 | year=2005 | issn=0032-079X | doi=10.1007/s11104-004-2390-x | pages=227–241| bibcode=2005PlSoi.271..227M | hdl=20.500.11850/32245 | s2cid=45517108 | hdl-access=free }}</ref> It could also be demonstrated that the biodegradable chelant [[EDDS]] can be used to enhance [[Phytoremediation|phytoextraction]] of polluting metals by mobilizing the metals in the soil, although metal-EDDS complexes are less available for uptake by roots through the symplastic pathway than free metal ions.<ref name="Tandy Schulin Nowack pp. 2753–2758">{{cite journal | last1=Tandy | first1=Susan | last2=Schulin | first2=Rainer | last3=Nowack | first3=Bernd | title=Uptake of Metals during Chelant-Assisted Phytoextraction with EDDS Related to the Solubilized Metal Concentration | journal=Environmental Science & Technology | publisher=American Chemical Society (ACS) | volume=40 | issue=8 | date=14 March 2006 | issn=0013-936X | doi=10.1021/es052141c | pages=2753–2758| pmid=16683619 | bibcode=2006EnST...40.2753T }}</ref><ref name="Tandy Schulin Nowack 2006 pp. 1454–1463">{{cite journal | last1=Tandy | first1=Susan | last2=Schulin | first2=Rainer | last3=Nowack | first3=Bernd | title=The influence of EDDS on the uptake of heavy metals in hydroponically grown sunflowers | journal=Chemosphere | publisher=Elsevier BV | volume=62 | issue=9 | year=2006 | issn=0045-6535 | doi=10.1016/j.chemosphere.2005.06.005 | pages=1454–1463| pmid=16083944 | bibcode=2006Chmsp..62.1454T }}</ref>

Schulin et al. also showed how much care has to be taken in attributing soil pollution to specific sources. Detailed analyses of soil profiles revealed that – in contrast to the conclusions of previous investigations based on spatial distributions of topsoil metal concentrations – the majority of metals in the vicinity of a ferrous metal smelter were of geogenic origin.<ref name="Schulin Curchod Mondeshka Daskalova 2007 pp. 52–61">{{cite journal | last1=Schulin | first1=Rainer | last2=Curchod | first2=Fabien | last3=Mondeshka | first3=Margarita | last4=Daskalova | first4=Angelina | last5=Keller | first5=Armin | title=Heavy metal contamination along a soil transect in the vicinity of the iron smelter of Kremikovtzi (Bulgaria) | journal=Geoderma | publisher=Elsevier BV | volume=140 | issue=1–2 | year=2007 | issn=0016-7061 | doi=10.1016/j.geoderma.2007.03.007 | pages=52–61| bibcode=2007Geode.140...52S }}</ref>

Also in contrast to previous belief that macropores invariably are the most compaction-sensitive types of soil pores Schulin and teamworkers showed that this only holds for packing voids between soil aggregates, whereas cylindrical macropores are in fact much more robust than bulk soil against deformation by compaction.<ref name="Schäffer Stauber Mueller Müller 2008 pp. 183–191">{{cite journal | last1=Schäffer | first1=B. | last2=Stauber | first2=M. | last3=Mueller | first3=T.L. | last4=Müller | first4=R. | last5=Schulin | first5=R. | title=Soil and macro-pores under uniaxial compression. I. Mechanical stability of repacked soil and deformation of different types of macro-pores | journal=Geoderma | publisher=Elsevier BV | volume=146 | issue=1–2 | year=2008 | issn=0016-7061 | doi=10.1016/j.geoderma.2008.05.019 | pages=183–191| bibcode=2008Geode.146..183S }}</ref> [[Neutron radiography]] was proved as a powerful tool to simultaneously determine soil water content and root development in soil.<ref name="Moradi Conesa Robinson Lehmann pp. 243–255">{{cite journal | last1=Moradi | first1=Ahmad B. | last2=Conesa | first2=Héctor M. | last3=Robinson | first3=Brett | last4=Lehmann | first4=Eberhard | last5=Kuehne | first5=Guido | last6=Kaestner | first6=Anders | last7=Oswald | first7=Sascha | last8=Schulin | first8=Rainer | title=Neutron radiography as a tool for revealing root development in soil: capabilities and limitations | journal=Plant and Soil | publisher=Springer Science and Business Media LLC | volume=318 | issue=1–2 | date=9 December 2008 | issn=0032-079X | doi=10.1007/s11104-008-9834-7 | pages=243–255| hdl=20.500.11850/11240 | s2cid=40794070 | hdl-access=free }}</ref>

==Memberships==
{{BLP unreferenced section|date=August 2023}}
* Associate Editor of the ''Journal of Environmental Quality'', 2005-2011
* Expert for the ''German Research Foundation'' (DFG), in particular in the expert boards of DFG priority research programmes.
* Evaluation panels of various research programs of the ''Swiss National Science Foundation'' (SNSF)
* Committee of the ''Swiss Soil Science Society'', 1998-2004, including two years as president.
* Executive Board of the ''International Society of Trace Element Biogeochemistry'' (ISTEB), 2003–2007
